title: Why quantum entanglement defies local realism
dek: How correlated measurements at a distance forced physicists to rethink locality.
sentences: Classical physics assumes that physical objects possess definite properties even when nobody is measuring them.
It also assumes locality, meaning that an event in one location cannot instantly affect a distant location without a physical signal.
Quantum entanglement shatters these comfortable intuitive assumptions about physical reality.
When two particles are generated in an entangled state, their physical properties become inextricably linked into a single wave function.
Measuring the spin of one particle instantly reveals the spin state of its entangled twin, regardless of the distance separating them.
Albert Einstein argued that this apparent connection implied the particles carried hidden variables decided beforehand.
Decades later, physicist John Bell showed mathematically that local hidden variables produce measurement correlations bounded by a strict limit.
Repeated laboratory experiments demonstrated that quantum particles routinely violate Bell's inequality limits.
This violation proves that physical reality cannot be both strictly local and predetermined before measurement.
Crucially, entanglement cannot be used to transmit messages faster than light, because individual measurement outcomes remain completely random.
Physicists must therefore accept that nature allows non-local correlations while strictly preserving the relativistic speed limit for information.

keyPoints.statement: Entangled particles share a single wave function such that measuring one instantly reveals the other regardless of distance.
keyPoints.addHint: Explain entanglement: particles share a single state so measuring one immediately gives information about the other across any distance.
keyPoints.example: Entangled particles share a unified wave function, so measuring the spin of one immediately reveals the state of the other no matter how far apart they are.

keyPoints.concept: Bell inequality rules out local realism
keyPoints.statement: Violations of Bell's inequalities prove that physical reality cannot be explained by local hidden variables decided in advance.
keyPoints.addHint: Describe Bell's theorem: experiments violate Bell's inequality limits, ruling out local hidden variables that determine outcomes beforehand.
keyPoints.example: Experiments show entangled particles violate Bell's inequalities, proving that nature cannot be explained by local hidden variables.

keyPoints.statement: Entanglement does not transmit faster-than-light messages because individual measurement outcomes are entirely random.
keyPoints.addHint: Point out the communication limit: because individual measurement results are random, entanglement cannot transmit faster-than-light signals.
keyPoints.example: Entanglement cannot send messages faster than light because each measurement result is completely random on its own.

commonMisconceptions.statement: Entanglement allows instantaneous communication across space
commonMisconceptions.why: Measurement outcomes are inherently random, so no information can be sent faster than light.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Entanglement does not enable faster-than-light communication because individual measurement results are completely random.

commonMisconceptions.statement: Einstein was proven right about local hidden variables
commonMisconceptions.why: Experiments consistently violated Bell's inequalities, disproving local hidden variable theories.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Bell tests proved Einstein's local hidden variable hypothesis wrong by showing quantum correlations violate classical limits.

samples.label: Clear explanation
samples.text: The article explains why quantum entanglement challenges our intuition about physical reality. When two particles become entangled, they share a single wave function, meaning measuring one instantly reveals the state of the other across any distance. Einstein thought particles carried hidden variables decided in advance. However, John Bell proved that local hidden variables have mathematical limits, and experiments consistently violate Bell's inequalities. This rules out local realism. Still, entanglement cannot send faster-than-light messages because each measurement outcome is completely random.

samples.label: Contains a misconception
samples.text: Quantum entanglement allows instant communication across space. When two particles are entangled, scientists can change one particle's spin and instantly send messages faster than light to the other particle on Mars. Einstein was right that particles have preset values that explain everything locally without breaking physics.
